steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Place rhubarb in a large mixing bowl. Add white sugar and 3 tablespoons flour; stir well to coat and spread evenly in the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Set aside.
Combine 1 ½ cups flour, brown sugar, and oats in a separate mixing bowl; cut in butter until the mixture is crumbly. Sprinkle crumble mixture over rhubarb layer.
Bake in the preheated oven until rhubarb filling is bubbling and crumble on top is golden brown, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Rhubarb Crunch
raw_recipe.description: This rhubarb crunch has a tender and juicy layer of tart rhubarb with a sweet and buttery oat crumble on top that bakes up golden brown and delicious.

video.description: This delicious rhubarb crumble is easy to make and will surely delight your friends and family.

review.reviewBody: I altered this one. I increased rhubarb to 6 cups, the sugar by half a cup and then added a pint of strawberries and a peach, which really adds to the overall flavor. Everyone went nuts over this one. Our house came with an 80 year old rhubarb plant, this was the first recipie I tried for it. Will be making this one, again!

This is a basic recipe that needs some tweaking to your preference. Personally, we love the tartness of rhubarb, I reduced the sugar in both parts. I picked and diced 10 lbs of rhubarb. I doubled the recipe to make 4 cake pans as gifts. The measurements I used were: 3 cups rolled oats, 3 cups flour, 1 1/2 cups brown sugar, 1 cup melted butter, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp powdered vanilla. For the rhubarb 18 cups (4.5 lbs) diced rhubarb, 1 1/2 cups white sugar and 1/2 cup flour. I baked in my convection oven at 350 for 30 minutes. Served with vanilla ice cream

This is a very easy recipe to put together. I used gluten free flour and non-dairy shortening. 've served it twice and people loved it. 
I made one change the second time. I drained the liquid that accumulates under the raw rhubarb-sugar mixture, thickened it with a little cornstarch and folded it back into the rhubarb before spreading it on the bottom crumble. This prevented the juice from soaking into the crumble , keeping the crumble more crisp and the rhubarb layer more distinct. Either way, it's delicious!

Turned out wonderful! I've never used rhubarb before but remember my Mom used to make a pie so I had to give it a try. I didn't have enough rhubarb to make a pie so I looked and this recipe sounded good. There was only about 2/3 of the rhubarb required. I cut all the ingredients down to 2/3 and uses a 9×9 pan. The fruit still looked a little lacking. Other reviews suggested several different kinds of fruit to add. I had a can of peaches. I drained the juice and mixed them into the rhubarb. Still using the 9×9 pan. It turned out perfect!

I added 8 cups of chopped rhubarb , 6 tablespoons of flour (4 white and 2 wheat) and 1 1/3 cups of sugar to the rhubarb.-next time I might add 1 1/2 cups of sugar. To the topping I added a quarter teaspoon of salt and a teaspoon of cinnamon and a half cup of chopped slightly toasted nuts. I think you could reduce the butter to 1 1/2 sticks or 3/4 cups. That being said, the topping with the original amount of butter is crunchy like the recipe's name. If you only use one stick of butter you may get a good crumble on the top, but it won't be as crunchy. The crunchy top also stands up better to the moisture from the rhubarb so the topping stays crunchy rather than turning to mush if you keep it overnight. Don't forget this does NOT have to be refrigerated if you keep it for a couple of days.
This is delicious. I did use 6 cups of rhubarb, 1 1/4 C sugar and 4 Tbsp flour.

I have made this many times. Today, tweaked the recipe by doubling rolled oats, and increasing butter proportionally to give it a toothier texture. Also sweetened the rhubarb with Monk Fruit sugar, 1 f9r 1. Otherwise the same recipe. It came out great!
It was way to thin using a 9x13 dish. Used a smaller dish for a thicker end product. Reduced the amount of sugar by half.

As I write this review my rhubarb is plotting to overthrow the squash and tomatoes in my garden. In other words, I have a lot of rhubarb and am always on the lookout for recipes that only use rhubarb. I have made this dessert several times and it is the one crisp dessert my husband requests as he prefers pie. I also double the amount of rhubarb called for in the recipe, use the same amount of sugar, and use half the amount of topping, which is personal preference. The proportions of ingredients in the topping is excellent no matter how much you should decide to make. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

I loved this recipe, and I did change it as some other people had suggested, added six cups total of fruit two cups of raspberries from my garden and four cups of rhubarb. I lowered the flower to one cup only used a half cup of butter and I did use one and one quarter cup of sugar which made it a little too sweet I think so next time it will be one cup and I think it will be perfect! This is a super recipe I've seen many times very similar and is the essence of spring than summer

My mother made a great rhubarb pie, my pies not so great. When we sold her house, we transplanted some rhubarb to our backyard. It grew really well, and we never used it all. I discovered this recipe a few years ago, and now we always use or freeze all of it. 

I doubled the amount of rhubarb because we love it. I have also reduced the butter and flour in the crunchand doubled the oats. As another reviewer said, those are personal preferences. this is a great recipe!
I would add more sugar next time.
Changes ...Used 4 cups rhubard and used only 1/2 white sugar... I sprinkled alittle cinnamon sugar on top before baking. Perfect tartness. Delicious!!
Easy to make and tasts great
I made it gluten free flour and added cinnamon to the mix.
It’s really good. I had 5 longish stalks of rhubarb, so I used an 8x8” pan. Cut the white sugar in half, but made the rest the same as recipe.
Really liked this but thinking needs more fruit. Likely a good 4 cups of rhubarb and cut the sugar. Still very tasty as is! It’s a keeper
Please stop rating this 4/5 stars and comment that for it to be good you have to double the fruit or halve the topping. It’s inedible in the current proportions.
Quick and easy. Great with ice cream.
Made it just like the recipe said let it cool a little and then put it still warm on vanilla ice cream. Yummy!
